issues.title: 2.2 Position my forces - move draggable logic
issues.body:
Currently, we have logic in `index.js` that controls if an asset is draggable.

But, the relevant MapPhasePlayerListener module is a better place to determine whether a particular marker should be draggable in this game phase.

So, remove the `assetIsDraggable` element from `index.js` -> `markerFor` logic.  `markerFor` should not make any markers draggable.

The `MapAdjudicationPendingListener` class should check if the asset is of my force, and has the 'locationPending' flag assigned. If it does, it should be draggable.

issues.title: Infrastructure - deliver OpenSeaMap
issues.body:
The client likes how the OpenStreetMap backdrop layer allows them to run a wargame anywhere on the globe.

They would be grateful if we could provide an OpenStreetMap (or OpenSeaMap) instance on their network.

This would require:
* get the OSM dataset
* load the OSM dataset into a PostGis database
* provide a map-server over PostGis, serving the OSM tiles

Here are the steps to create an OpenStreetMap tile server:
https://www.linuxbabe.com/ubuntu/openstreetmap-tile-server-ubuntu-18-04-osm

Note: OpenSeaMap is a maritime extension to OpenStreetMap, but it doesn't appear to share it's underlying data as much, and an inspection of the Irish Sea suggests it doesn't bring any additional data of value.

issues.title: Move back to monolith
issues.body:
Early in the project lifetime we moved from a monolith to a mono-repo

But, except for the (very-small) server-side component it really is just one app.    It is also built, distributed, and run as one app.

We should consider returning to a monolith repo.

### Pros
- It would avoid the multiple version numbers spread across the repo
- simpler build process
- simpler architecture

### Cons
- could be a lot of effort
- we will lose ability to run `build` on just one component (`helpers` rebuilds really quickly)
